newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Malaysian PM foresees more investment in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian PM foresees more investment in Pakistan.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Wednesday he believed Pakistan's liberal economic policies would attract greater investment from his country.

Speaking at a banquet with Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif at the end of a brief visit to Islamabad, he said both countries were well placed to be gateways for each other's products in their respective regions.

He earlier held talks with Sharif after arriving from a visit to Kuwait and Bahrain. A Pakistani spokesman said the Malaysian expressed eagerness to begin joint ventures with Pakistan and remove their existing trade imbalance that favours Kuala Lumpur.

Mahathir told a news conference before leaving for Kuala Lumpur that Malaysia would help Islamabad get full dialogue partnership with the Association of South East Asian Nations and to join the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum -- two groups of which Malaysia is member.
He said in his speech he believed that Sharif's recent economic revival package would "create opportunities paving the way for greater Malaysian investments in Pakistan".
"Malaysia-Pakistan joint ventures would contribute towards bringing about a more desirable balance in the area of trade and payments between our two countries," he said.
Nine Malaysian companies have already invested in Pakistan in oil and gas exploration, port storage and bulking installation, telecommunications and tyre-related industry.

Mahathir said Malaysia was interested and ready to participate in other sectors of development in Pakistan such as infrastructure, housing and construction, finance and banking, electronics and computers.

The current trade balance is heavily tilted in favour of Malaysia, from where Pakistan imports most of its palm oil requirements. The volume of two-way trade in fiscal 1995-96 (July-June) was $850 million.

Mahathir also showed great interest in Malaysia's "participation in joint venture collaboration with Pakistan and also in the possibility of relocating labour intensive industries from Malaysia to Pakistan," Pakistan foreign ministry official Shamshad Ahmad told reporters.
